### Diagnosis

The current bug report describes an issue where `ClassUtils.getShortClassName()` is adding a semicolon at the end of class names for arrays. This issue is demonstrated in the failing test case where the assertion for an array class name fails when checking the short class name.

By inspecting the `getShortClassName` method in the `ClassUtils` class, it is evident that the method handles array encoding in a way that may lead to the addition of a semicolon. The method extracts the class name from the input string and sets it as the output after certain manipulations. In the case of arrays, it may not handle the array encoding correctly, leading to the incorrect output with a semicolon at the end of the class name.

To fix this issue, the handling of array encoding needs to be adjusted in the `getShortClassName` method to ensure that the proper class name is extracted without any unintended characters added.

### Best Fix Locations
- `org.apache.commons.lang.ClassUtils.getShortClassName(java.lang.String)`

Would you like to continue with further information or actions?

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
